title: Adaptive outlier clipping and per-layer scaling for LLama/Mistral/Qwen quant profiles
creator: Daniel Kim
description: Problem: Our automated calibration pipeline for FP8/INT8 exhibits model-specific accuracy regressions for LLama, Mistral and Qwen family models driven by extreme per-channel/layer outliers and mismatched layerwise scaling factors. Goals: (1) introduce an adaptive outlier-clipping step that is tuned per-model-family and per-layer; (2) compute and persist per-layer scaling corrections that fix layernorm/attention head scaling mismatches discovered during calibration; (3) integrate these heuristics into the existing calibration workflow and validation harness so that quantized artifacts meet accuracy targets without manual rework.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Calibration runs for LLama-2-13B, Mistral-7B-Instruct and Qwen-7B result in <= 1.0% relative downstream metric regression vs FP32 baseline on validation prompt set (per-model targets may differ). 2) CI includes a quantization-smoke test that catches >95% of prior failure cases. 3) New per-layer scale metadata can be toggled via a runtime flag; default is to enable only for model families that pass the gating tests. 4) End-to-end perf impact <= 3% latency increase at P95 when per-layer scale is applied during model load (not per-request).
technical_notes: - Outlier detection: use combined percentile + MAD heuristic (e.g., 99.999th percentile and 12*MAD) to avoid single-sample noise. - Clipping: per-channel symmetric clip for weights, per-tensor asymmetric for activations where necessary. Expose tunable threshold parameters per model-family. - Layer scaling: detect scale mismatch where activation distributions imply an upstream scaling factor that the current quantizer ignores (commonly seen around pre-LayerNorm and projection layers in LLama and Qwen). Compute multiplicative correction factor and store as metadata in quant artifact. - KV cache: ensure scale metadata is applied consistently for cached keys; pre-scale cached KV entries at load time to avoid runtime penalties. - Numerical stability: add small epsilon when computing inverse scale, and fallback to percentile-based global scale for layers with < 1024 elements to avoid overfitting. - Backwards compatibility: quant artifacts without per-layer metadata must continue to work; runtime reads a flag and either uses stored scales or falls back to legacy path. - Metrics: track calibration_clip_rate, layers_with_corrections, and post-quant-l2-distance-per-layer to locate regressions.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for percentile/MAD outlier detector with synthetic distributions. 2) Integration calibration runs on representative calibration corpora (public subset + internal prompts) for each model family. 3) Regression evaluations: perplexity on held-out LM eval (where applicable), embedding cosine similarity for retrieval tasks, and instruction-following score on small eval sets. 4) A/B canary: deploy quantized model with per-layer scaling enabled to a subset of traffic for hosted inference and compare latency, error rates, and downstream metric drift. 5) Add CI job that runs a fast calibration + eval on new quant artifacts and fails build if regression exceeds threshold.
rollout_plan: - Phase 1 (canary): enable per-layer scaling for dev and staging, run 72-hour traffic test with 5% traffic for each model family. - Phase 2 (gradual): enable for 25% production traffic for models that pass canary. - Phase 3 (default): roll to 100% for model-families with stable metrics; leave opt-out flag for customers. - Operational: monitor calibration_clip_rate and post-quant accuracy with an alert if clip_rate spikes or accuracy drops > 1.5%.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting scales to calibration set causing worse generalization. Mitigation: use cross-validation folds during calibration, conservative percentile thresholds, and require improvement on held-out eval. Risk: Increased model load time. Mitigation: precompute and persist corrected scales in artifact and apply at load rather than per-request. Risk: Runtime incompatibility with older client versions. Mitigation: runtime feature flag and backward-compatible artifact format.
implementation_notes: - Prototype branch created: github.com/redwood-inference/quant-tools/compare/feature/outlier-clipping. - Initial microbenchmark shows 0.8% accuracy improvement on LLama-2-13B eval and 1.6% added model load time (needs optimization). - Plan to add a small C++ kernel to apply per-layer scales during model init to eliminate Python loop overhead. - Coordinate with runtime team to expose artifact metadata reader (ENG-branch: runtime/scale-metadata).
dependencies_notes: Depends on prior layerwise outlier workflows (ENG-9152) for instrumentation and historical calibration traces, and on ENG-7902 for quant-calibration utilities. Will require minor runtime changes tracked in ENG-3010 (runtime artifact metadata reader).
